name: Perplexity Health Connector Marketplace proposal
why: Perplexity Health (launched 19 March 2026) brings wearable data from Fitbit, Ultrahuman, Withings and Apple Health into personalised health answers, and the Perplexity Help Center invites companies to propose new connectors through a form or connectors@perplexity.ai. Nightly HR, HRV and sleep timing compared with a personal baseline is the kind of context those answers draw on.
why_now: Perplexity Health launched on 19 March 2026 and the 27 March 2026 changelog rolled it out to Pro and Max subscribers in the US; the connector proposal article is live in the Help Center now.
channel: Connector proposal form in the Perplexity Help Center, or email connectors@perplexity.ai with company, use case and API docs (connectors@perplexity.ai)
warm_path: Wearable connectors run on Terra API, which is already on the board; a Terra listing gives a second route in alongside a direct proposal.
ask: Send a short connector proposal for Vybe nightly data (HR, HRV, sleep timing against personal baseline) and ask whether they prefer a direct connector or the Terra route.
opener: Hi Perplexity Connectors team, I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health in Raleigh. Perplexity Health launched in March with Fitbit, Ultrahuman and Withings connectors, and your Help Center now invites connector proposals. We're developing a screenless overnight band that reads heart rate, HRV and sleep timing and compares each night to the wearer's own baseline, plus a developer SDK. When it's ready I'd be glad to send early SDK docs and sample overnight data so your team can judge the fit. Would you rather see a direct connector proposal from us, or should we come in through Terra? https://calendly.com/jeremy-vybe/30min
opportunity: Become a Perplexity Health wearable connector (direct or via Terra) so members can ask about their own overnight baseline.

name: IEEE P1752 Open Mobile Health Working Group (P1752.2 CardioRespiratory and Sleep subgroups)
role: Working group mailing list (1752-wg via ListServ@ieee.org)
why: P1752 publishes open schemas for mobile health data; P1752.2 covers cardiovascular, respiratory and metabolic measures, with wearable makers and data aggregators named as stakeholders, and there is a Sleep subgroup. Joining is by subscribing to the 1752-wg listserv. Mapping Vybe's SDK output to these schemas would make it easier for aggregators to take in.
why_now: The working group posted slides and minutes for calls throughout 2026 (6 January to 22 September); the next CardioRespiratory subgroup call is 22 October 2026 and the next working group call is 3 November 2026.
channel: Email ListServ@ieee.org with subject 1752-wg and body 'subscribe 1752-wg FirstName LastName', then post to the list (ListServ@ieee.org)
warm_path: Open mHealth lineage; the group's own pages list openmhealth.org contacts, but no named person is greeted.

ice.note: Free listserv join; low effort, builds standards credibility with aggregators.

ask: Subscribe to 1752-wg, listen in on the 22 October CardioRespiratory subgroup call, and offer Vybe overnight HR, HRV and sleep timing fields as a test case for P1752.2 schemas.
opener: Hello P1752 working group, I'm Jeremy, founder of Vybe Health in Raleigh. I've been reading the P1752.2 cardiorespiratory work and your 2026 meeting minutes, most recently September 22. We're developing a screenless overnight band that reads heart rate, HRV and sleep timing and compares each night to the wearer's own baseline, plus a developer SDK, and we'd like our data to map cleanly to your schemas. Once ready I'd be glad to share early SDK docs and sample overnight data as a test case. Would the cardiorespiratory subgroup welcome a new wearable maker listening in on October 22? https://calendly.com/jeremy-vybe/30min
